Lee told Wang that China and South Korea have achieved tangible results toward a "full restoration" of bilateral ties, pledging to support China's effort in hosting the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen later this year, his office said. South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun told Parliament that the ministry was [USN:L1N44G0CJ TEXT:"pursuing a summit"] between Lee and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the summit.

item.title: Israël met en garde la Turquie contre toute "aventure dangereuse" en Syrie
item.description: Le ministre israélien de la Défense, Israel Katz, a déclaré jeudi que le président turc Recep Tayyip Erdogan entraînait la Turquie dans "des aventures dangereuses en Syrie", et qu'Israël ne permettrait à aucune entité de menacer sa propre sécurité.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le ministre israélien de la Défense, Israel Katz, a déclaré jeudi que le président turc Recep Tayyip Erdogan entraînait la Turquie dans "des aventures dangereuses en Syrie", et qu'Israël ne permettrait à aucune entité de menacer sa propre sécurité. Les relations entre la Turquie et Israël, dégradées en raison d'échanges de plus en plus vifs au sujet de la Syrie - où les armées des deux pays sont actives - se sont davantage détériorées cette semaine, alors que l'Etat hébreu a frappé une base militaire syrienne proche de la frontière turque. Israël a frappé [USN:L8N44F0JE TEXT:"mardi"] la base aérienne militaire d'Abou Douhour, dans le nord-ouest de la Syrie, estimant que Damas était sur le point de violer un "statu quo convenu avec Israël en matière de sécurité" en autorisant le déploiement de troupes turques sur cette base. Sur X, Israel Katz a déclaré que Recep Tayyip Erdogan ferait mieux de se retenir de tester la détermination d'Israël à se défendre. "Israël ne permettra à aucun acteur de menacer sa sécurité", a-t-il dit. Mais le ministre syrien des Affaires étrangères, Asaad al-Chaibani, a déclaré avoir clairement fait savoir à Israël qu’il n’était pas prévu d’établir une base militaire turque en Syrie et que le site d'Abou Douhour était en cours de réhabilitation pour être utilisé par l’armée de l’air syrienne. "Il n’y avait aucune intention d’y établir une base turque, ni d’y instaurer une présence militaire turque permanente, ni de déployer des forces turques sur le site", a-t-il dit mercredi lors d’un entretien avec Axios. La Turquie a quant à elle mercredi [USN:L6N44G0J8 TEXT:"fermement rejeté"] les "allégations indéfendables" d'Israël concernant sa présence militaire en Syrie, estimant que le Premier ministre israélien Benjamin Netanyahu cherchait à mener des "politiques expansionnistes et déstabilisantes". Le ministère turc de la Défense a déclaré jeudi qu’aucune délégation militaire turque n’était présente sur la base avant ou pendant la frappe, et que la Turquie continuerait à soutenir les efforts de la Syrie visant à développer ses propres capacités et infrastructures militaires. "Il est essentiel, pour la paix et la stabilité tant de la Syrie que de la région, qu’Israël mette fin à ces attaques imprudentes et se conforme aux exigences du droit international", a-t-il déclaré. AUCUNE JUSTIFICATION LÉGITIME POUR CES FRAPPES, ESTIME DAMAS La Turquie, qui dispose de la deuxième plus grande armée de l'Otan, s’est imposée comme l’un des principaux alliés du président syrien Ahmed al Charaa, au pouvoir depuis la chute de Bachar al Assad en décembre 2024. Ankara, qui accuse Israël de tenter de déstabiliser la Syrie et de saper sa nouvelle administration, appelle à exercer une pression internationale sur l'Etat hébreu pour l'obliger à respecter l’intégrité territoriale de son voisin. Les inquiétudes d'Israël vis-à-vis de la Syrie, concernaient autrefois l'influence iranienne à Damas mais sont désormais orientées autour du rôle de la Turquie aux côtés d'Ahmed al Charaa. Benjamin Netanyahu a déclaré mercredi qu’Israël avait averti la Syrie de ne pas autoriser de présence turque sur la base d'Abou Douhour. "Notre message était très clair : ne le faites pas. Je suppose qu’ils n’ont pas tout à fait compris le message", a déclaré mercredi le Premier ministre israélien. Asaad al-Chaibani a déclaré qu’Israël n’avait aucune justification légitime pour ce bombardement. Il a ajouté que des officiers militaires turcs s’étaient rendus sur la base dans le cadre d’une formation et d’une coopération militaire plus large. Il a nié tout renforcement militaire turc, affirmant que l’installation était en grande partie vide et n’était pas encore opérationnelle. Des sources ont indiqué mercredi à Reuters que la question des déploiements militaires turcs en Syrie avait été abordée lors d’un rare entretien téléphonique entre Asaad al-Chaibani et le chef des services secrets israéliens (Mossad), Roman Gofman, le 14 août, quelques jours avant la frappe. L’année dernière, la Turquie et Israël — également en profond désaccord sur la guerre à Gaza — ont établi une ligne de communication afin d’éviter tout incident en Syrie. Tom Barrack, l’envoyé spécial du président américain pour la Syrie et l’Irak, a déclaré à Reuters après les frappes de mardi que Washington s’efforçait de mettre en place un mécanisme de prévention des conflits entre Israël, la Turquie et la Syrie. Damas reste par ailleurs ouvert à des négociations avec Israël sur la désescalade, a déclaré Asaad al-Chaibani. Les deux parties avaient réalisé des progrès significatifs vers un accord de sécurité après des pourparlers menés sous l’égide des États-Unis, mais Israël s’est rétracté de ses engagements et l’accord n’a pas été mis en œuvre, a-t-il ajouté. Le ministre syrien a déclaré que tout accord futur devait répondre aux préoccupations de sécurité des deux parties et respecter la souveraineté syrienne, avertissant que la poursuite des opérations militaires israéliennes ne ferait qu’accroître l’instabilité régionale.

item.title: North Korea launches 10 ballistic missiles as US-South Korea drills near end
item.description: South Korea's presidential office condemned North Korea's launch of more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles on Thursday and ordered its military to maintain full readiness during ongoing joint exercises with the United States.
item.dc:creator: Joyce Lee, Kyu-Seok Shim
item.content:encoded: South Korea's presidential office condemned North Korea's launch of more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles on Thursday and ordered its military to maintain full readiness during ongoing joint exercises with the United States. The launch came after North Korea's [USN:L1N44G0IC TEXT:"Kim Yo Jong"], sister of Kim Jong Un, on Wednesday condemned the U.S.-South Korea military drills, despite U.S. President Donald Trump's order to substantially reduce U.S. participation in the exercises. The presidential office convened an emergency security meeting attended by officials from the defence ministry and military authorities after North Korea fired the missiles from the Pyongyang area toward the sea to the east of the Korean Peninsula, it said in a statement. "The ballistic missile launch is a grave act that violates U.N. Security Council resolutions," it said, calling on North Korea to immediately halt such actions. The missiles flew around 300 kilometres (186 miles) toward the sea, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said. South Korean defence minister Ahn Gyu-back told lawmakers that the short-range ballistic missiles are believed to be 600 mm multiple rocket launchers, adding that Seoul has been tracking them because they could be potentially deployed near its border with the South. North Korea has previously described the 600 mm system, known externally as the KN-25, as being able to deliver tactical nuclear warheads. Ahn said earlier in the day that North Korea possesses between 80 and 120 nuclear warheads. Military drills by South Korea and the U.S. were [USN:L1N44G018 TEXT:"cut short"] to end on Friday after President Donald Trump ordered a substantial reduction in U.S. participation and said he wanted to revive diplomacy with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. Trump said on Monday he had received a response from North Korean leader Kim Jong Un after the reduction. But Kim's sister, [USN:L1N44G0IC TEXT:"Kim Yo Jong"], said on Wednesday she was unaware of any recent communications between the two countries' leaders, while saying the United States' "hostile policy" towards North Korea had not changed. Yang Moo-jin, a professor at the University of North Korean Studies in Seoul, said the launch appeared aimed at underscoring that Kim Yo Jong's warning a day earlier was "not mere rhetoric." He said the launch likely served multiple purposes, including signalling opposition to the South Korea-U.S. military exercises, expressing displeasure over recent discussion of North Korea's nuclear arsenal, and warning outside powers against speculation about Pyongyang's security affairs. "It is a message that matters concerning North Korea's security are for North Korea to decide," Yang said, adding the launch could also have been used to test improved missile systems. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, who visited Seoul this week, urged South Korea [USN:L1N44H09B TEXT:"not to take sides"] between Beijing and Washington, saying the U.S. should abandon its "hostile" policy toward North Korea to ease tensions on the Korean Peninsula.

item.title: Prince Harry and Meghan to make shock return to Britain after moving to US
item.description: Prince Harry and his wife Meghan plan to move back to Britain this month, six years after they quit royal duties and relocated to the U.S., from where they repeatedly criticised the royal family and lambasted the British press.
item.dc:creator: Michael Holden, Lisa Richwine
item.content:encoded: Prince Harry and his wife Meghan plan to move back to Britain this month, [USN:L1N44G14R TEXT:"six years after they quit royal duties"] and relocated to the U.S., from where they repeatedly criticised the royal family and lambasted the British press. A person close to the couple said they would move from California to somewhere outside London for an extended period with their children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, who will go to school in Britain. The surprise news marks the latest twist for a couple who railed against a string of British institutions after they left in 2020, with Harry accusing the royals of neglect, the tabloid press of ruining his life and the government of failing to provide enough security for him to ever return home. King Charles, who media reports said welcomed having his youngest son and his family closer, only found out about the move on Sunday. Harry and Meghan will not live in a royal residence and will remain non-working royals, as agreed with the late Queen Elizabeth. Harry's spokesperson and Buckingham Palace declined to comment. COUPLE COMPLAINED ABOUT PRESS COVERAGE Harry married Meghan Markle at Windsor Castle in 2018, and it was hoped his union with the former actor would reinvigorate the historic institution for a new generation. But it was not long before cracks in their relationship with the rest of the royal family began to emerge. Two years later in March 2020, they announced they would step down from official duties and move to the U.S., saying they wanted to leave behind the [USN:L8N44H0TT TEXT:""toxic" press scrutiny"] they faced in Britain. They settled in the wealthy seaside enclave of Montecito, near Santa Barbara, California, with media reports putting the 2020 purchase price of their 16-bedroom home at $14.7 million, a property which they will keep. In the following years, Harry, now 41, and Meghan, 45, repeatedly hit out at the royal family and the monarchy in TV interviews, a Netflix (NFLX.O) documentary series and, most notably, in Harry's memoir "Spare". During a 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey, Meghan, whose mother is Black, said an unnamed member of the family had asked [USN:L9N2JH00B TEXT:"how dark"] their son Archie’s skin might be. Heir-to-the-throne Prince William, Harry's elder brother, responded by denying that Britain’s royals were racist. Harry also had some particularly barbed comments for his father Charles, and William, leading to a total breakdown in their relationship. He later criticised the British government after it changed his security arrangements and said the lack of automatic police protection meant he was unable to bring his children to Britain. STRAINED FAMILY RELATIONS But relations with the king, who is undergoing treatment for an unspecified cancer, appeared to be thawing in September, and father and son met briefly for the first time in 20 months. Last month, Harry, Meghan and their children visited Britain, and Charles saw his grandchildren for the first time since 2022. While Harry and the king's relationship might have improved, he is still barely on speaking terms with his brother. Harry had always said he wanted his children to spend more time in Britain but a former senior royal aide said the return would pose challenges for everyone involved, adding that royals who try to forge private careers are often accused by critics of exploiting their position. The former aide said the news would be particularly difficult for William and his wife Kate, after Harry and Meghan "dumped all over the institution, the members of the family, and the country from a great height for money". Prime Minister Andy Burnham, asked if the taxpayer would [USN:L1N42Y0EJ TEXT:"fund their security needs"], said it was a private matter for the couple and he wished them well. COMMENTATOR SAYS THEY WILL PREPARE FOR MEDIA Harry and Meghan embarked on several media ventures from their California home, signing multi-million-dollar deals with Spotify (SPOT.N) for a podcast series and with Netflix for programming including a lifestyle show hosted by Meghan. The projects produced mixed results. Harry's tell-all book was a bestseller, but their podcast deal ended and Meghan's Netflix show was not renewed for a third season. In recent months, Meghan, who has launched a lifestyle brand, has published an increasing number of photographs on her Instagram account, showing Harry and their children and their U.S. life, often taken from behind the children to hide their faces. "They didn't achieve the superstar status they wanted," said Dominic Patten, executive editor of Hollywood publication Deadline.com, adding however that they had kept the public interested for a long time, which is not easy in a town full of big-name celebrities. Royal commentator Afua Hagan said that interest would ramp up in Britain as they return, with newspapers wanting to know where they would live and where the children would go to school. She said while they were essentially walking back in to the "lion's den" they were better prepared this time: "They're not bringing a knife to a gunfight. They know what they have to do, what they're going to come up against, and will prepare themselves better."

item.title: Deutsches Gastgewerbe befürchtet siebtes Minusjahr in Folge
item.description: Das deutsche Gastgewerbe hat im ersten Halbjahr einen deutlichen Rückgang der Einnahmen verkraften müssen. Inflationsbereinigt sank der Umsatz um 5,2 Prozent im Vergleich zum Vorjahreszeitraum, wie das Statistische Bundesamt am Donnerstag mitteilte. Durch Preiserhöhungen stieg der nominale Umsatz aber zugleich um 2,1 Prozent. Der Hotellerie- und Gastronomieverband (Dehoga) befürchtet nach dem mäßigen Auftakt das siebte Verlustjahr in Folge.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Das deutsche Gastgewerbe hat im ersten Halbjahr einen deutlichen Rückgang der Einnahmen verkraften müssen. Inflationsbereinigt sank der Umsatz um 5,2 Prozent im Vergleich zum Vorjahreszeitraum, wie das Statistische Bundesamt am Donnerstag mitteilte. Durch Preiserhöhungen stieg der nominale Umsatz aber zugleich um 2,1 Prozent. Der Hotellerie- und Gastronomieverband (Dehoga) befürchtet nach dem mäßigen Auftakt das siebte Verlustjahr in Folge. "Höhere Preise, mehr Abgaben und Steuern, wachsende Unsicherheiten und fehlende Perspektiven – all das dämpft die Konsumlaune", sagte die Dehoga-Hauptgeschäftsführerin Jana Schimke. "Und das bekommt das Gastgewerbe unmittelbar zu spüren." Viele Menschen sparten beim Ausgehen und beim Urlaub. Besonders angespannt ist die Lage in der Gastronomie. "Gäste kommen seltener, verzichten auf das Dessert oder das zweite Getränk", sagte Schimke. In der Gastronomie brach der reale Umsatz im ersten Halbjahr um 5,7 Prozent ein. Etwas milder fiel der Rückgang in der Hotellerie aus. Hotels und sonstige Beherbergungsunternehmen verzeichneten real 3,2 Prozent weniger Umsatz als im ersten Halbjahr 2025. Eine rasche Trendwende erwartet die Branche nicht. "Für das Gesamtjahr gibt es keinen Anlass zur Entwarnung", sagte Dehoga-Hauptgeschäftsführerin Schimke. "Selbst wenn die Sommermonate und das Weihnachtsgeschäft Impulse bringen, werden die enormen Verluste der ersten Jahreshälfte voraussichtlich nicht vollständig aufzuholen sein." Der Branche drohe das siebte Minusjahr in Folge. Ein gefährlicher Mix aus Konsumzurückhaltung und immer höheren Kosten werde für immer mehr Betriebe existenzgefährdend. Der überdurchschnittliche Anstieg der Insolvenzen im Gastgewerbe sei ein unübersehbares Alarmzeichen. Die Bundesregierung hatte der Branche unter die Arme gegriffen. Seit Jahresbeginn gilt der ermäßigte Mehrwertsteuersatz auf Speisen in der Gastronomie von sieben Prozent, nach zuvor 19 Prozent.

item.title: Ataques rusos dejan 16 muertos en Ucrania y Zelenski pide más interceptores Patriot
item.description: Ataques rusos causaron la muerte de 16 personas y dejaron más de 40 heridos en Kiev y sus alrededores el jueves, mientras el presidente Volodímir Zelenski decía que el hecho de que los aliados de Ucrania no repusieran sus existencias de misiles de defensa aérea estaba costando vidas.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Anna Pruchnicka
item.content:encoded: Ataques rusos causaron la muerte de 16 personas y dejaron más de 40 heridos en Kiev y sus alrededores el jueves, mientras el presidente Volodímir Zelenski decía que el hecho de que los aliados de Ucrania no repusieran sus existencias de misiles de defensa aérea estaba costando vidas. La Fuerza Aérea de Ucrania informó de que Rusia lanzó decenas de misiles balísticos, de crucero e hipersónicos, así como 168 drones, en el ataque masivo perpetrado durante la noche. La Fuerza Aérea dijo que casi el 90% de los drones y la mayoría de los misiles de crucero fueron derribados. No precisó cuántos misiles balísticos fueron lanzados, ni si alguno fue interceptado. Las plantas superiores de un bloque de viviendas de nueve pisos quedaron destruidas en el distrito de Solomianski, en Kiev, donde se produjeron la mayoría de las 15 muertes registradas en la capital, según el alcalde, Vitali Klitschko, que pidió que el viernes se considerara día de luto. Otros dos distritos sufrieron daños, según Klitschko, y resultaron afectados una escuela y un hospital infantil, así como instalaciones no residenciales y almacenes. El Ministerio de Defensa ruso dijo que Moscú atacó Kiev y la región circundante con ataques aéreos y drones, alcanzando instalaciones que producen componentes para drones, un depósito militar y un centro logístico, así como otros objetivos. ZELENSKI SOLICITA INTERCEPTORES PATRIOT Los ataques rusos también se dirigieron contra la región de Odesa, en el mar Negro, donde los repetidos ataques contra la infraestructura portuaria y los buques han paralizado prácticamente las exportaciones agrícolas vitales de Ucrania en las últimas semanas, lo que ha ejercido presión sobre los precios mundiales de los alimentos. Dado que Rusia ha intensificado sus ataques con misiles balísticos en los últimos meses, Zelenski ha instado a sus aliados a reponer las existencias de misiles interceptores Patriot de Ucrania, la única arma de su arsenal capaz de derribar un misil balístico. "Los misiles interceptores para los sistemas Patriot aún no han sido repuestos, y se necesitan cada día", dijo Zelenski en la aplicación Telegram. "Cada misil adicional salva la vida de nuestra gente". Según él, Moscú no negociará seriamente la paz mientras Ucrania no cuente con defensas antimisiles para proteger sus ciudades. Las conversaciones mediadas por EEUU para poner fin a la guerra, que ya dura cuatro años, se estancaron a principios de este año después de que Ucrania se negara a ceder a las exigencias rusas de renunciar a más territorios. "Por desgracia (…), la respuesta del mundo ante este tipo de ataques no siempre es la adecuada", dijo Zelenski. La presidenta de la Comisión Europea, Ursula von der Leyen, dijo en la red social X, en respuesta al mensaje de Zelenski, que estaba trabajando con los Estados miembros y los socios para proporcionar a Ucrania capacidades antibalísticas como "la prioridad más urgente". LAS EXPLOSIONES SACUDEN LA CAPITAL El primer ministro ucraniano, Serhi Koretski, dijo que algunos almacenes de alimentos y las instalaciones de la Cruz Roja en los alrededores de Kiev resultaron dañados en el ataque nocturno, que se prolongó durante casi nueve horas. En las últimas semanas, la fruta y la verdura frescas han desaparecido en ocasiones de las estanterías de algunos supermercados de la capital como consecuencia de los ataques contra los almacenes logísticos de las cadenas de distribución alimentaria. En el bloque de pisos dañado por un misil en el distrito de Solomianski, una anciana lloraba desconsoladamente mientras los equipos de rescate sacaban el cadáver de su nieto, según mostraban las imágenes de Reuters TV. Sollozaba de pie junto a su cadáver después de que lo depositaran en el suelo, antes de que los médicos se acercaran para consolarla. Aunque la mayoría de los fallecidos se registraron en la capital ucraniana, también murió una persona en la región circundante, según informó un responsable a través de Telegram. Ucrania también ha intensificado sus ataques contra Rusia, dirigiéndose contra instalaciones petroleras e infraestructuras logísticas para intentar socavar la capacidad de Moscú para librar la guerra. El mes pasado se registró el mayor número de víctimas civiles desde los primeros meses de la guerra, según la ONU, la mayoría de ellas en territorio ucraniano. Durante la noche, las autoridades de la región rusa de Tartaristán —a 1.000 kilómetros al este de Moscú— informaron de una interrupción en un complejo industrial de la ciudad de Nizhnekamsk tras un ataque con drones ucranianos, y añadieron que también resultaron dañados algunos edificios de viviendas. El Estado Mayor de Ucrania dijo que había atacado la refinería de petróleo TANECO y una terminal petrolera de la zona. Un dron se estrelló en Rumanía, miembro de la OTAN y de la Unión Europea, durante el ataque ruso contra Ucrania, según informó el jueves el Ministerio de Defensa rumano. También se estrelló un dron en territorio moldavo, según la presidenta del país, Maia Sandu. Ucrania ha entregado propuestas de paz a los negociadores estadounidenses, Steve Witkoff y Jared Kushner, para un plan destinado a poner fin a la guerra, según dijo Zelenski este mes. Rusia no recibió propuestas concretas para posibles nuevas reuniones con los negociadores estadounidenses, según dijo María Zajárova, portavoz del Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores ruso, al periódico Izvestia, aunque añadió que Moscú estaría dispuesta a organizar una reunión con poca antelación. Witkoff y Kushner estuvieron por última vez en Moscú el pasado mes de enero y aún no han visitado Kiev. Según una fuente familiarizada con las conversaciones, todavía no se ha confirmado ninguna fecha para la visita propuesta a Ucrania.

item.title: A decade after earthquake, Italy's Amatrice struggles to rebuild
item.description: In the early hours of August 24, 2016, Giorgio Cortellesi stumbled through the dust and darkness of Amatrice, fearing his children were dead, buried beneath tons of rubble.
item.dc:creator: Crispian Balmer
item.content:encoded: In the early hours of August 24, 2016, Giorgio Cortellesi stumbled through the dust and darkness of Amatrice, fearing his children were dead, buried beneath tons of rubble. His two young sons had been staying overnight with their grandparents when an earthquake levelled much of the central Italian hilltown. Rushing over from a nearby hamlet, Cortellesi found the streets in ruins, muffled cries rising from collapsed homes. Then he caught the sound of one of his sons calling for help. "I didn't think I would find them alive, but when I heard his voice, it was as if I started breathing again," said Cortellesi. He promised himself that if his boys survived he would help rebuild Amatrice, which bore the brunt of the calamity, with 237 people dying in the town out of a total death toll of 303. Elected town mayor in 2021, Cortellesi is trying to make good on his pledge, but it isn't easy. LIFE ON HOLD The 6.2-magnitude earthquake and aftershocks destroyed much of Amatrice's historic centre and many outlying areas, leaving several thousand people homeless. The state has promised to pay for the vast bulk of the reconstruction and has so far approved private and public sector projects worth €22.7 billion ($26.3 billion) across the disaster zone. Around €10 billion has been paid out to date. In Amatrice, 38% of the damaged properties have been restored, with the pace of building picking up markedly over the past 12 months. Cranes dot the town and clusters of pristine new homes have sprouted amidst the desolation. Even so, only a small proportion of the structures flattened in 2016 have been rebuilt. Much of the historic centre remains behind barriers, where two lone towers that survived the earthquake gaze over the blasted wasteland. Around 1,000 people, roughly 60% of the population, still live in small, prefabricated shelters, while each year a few families drift away, seeking a brighter future elsewhere. "After 10 years many people have lost faith," said Cortellesi. "We need to keep on encouraging them, but we can't do more than we are already doing." LONG ROAD BACK As with other major Italian earthquakes, such as L'Aquila in 2009, Amatrice's reconstruction got bogged down in bureaucracy, legal disputes and shifting priorities. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted rebuilding efforts, while Italy's generous "Superbonus" renovation scheme, intended to revive the virus-hit economy, pushed up the cost of building materials and siphoned off labour to more lucrative projects across Italy. "The Superbonus led to an almost total stop that lasted two years. It was a disaster," said Cortellesi. Rebuilding densely packed medieval neighbourhoods was complicated by multiple owners, inheritance disputes and unresolved property claims that made every planning application a legal minefield. Officials say fears of mafia interference in the adjudication of multi-million-euro contracts added further layers of scrutiny that snarled some projects for years. Yet for some survivors, the slow pace of reconstruction has been only one part of a much deeper struggle to remain. Daniele Bonanni lost his mother, sister and nephew in the earthquake, leaving just him, his niece and her baby daughter alive. A sought-after chef, Bonanni could easily have moved on. Instead he stayed put. "It seemed wrong to abandon the place where I grew up and where my family built a life," he said. "Perhaps it was a mistake. Even today I cannot say for certain." For years, descendants of Amatrice families returned each August to homes inherited from parents and grandparents, but many of those properties were lost. "People once came for the summer, now they come for lunch," said Bonanni, who runs a chic restaurant in a food village established for chefs who had lost their businesses. "If you create a generational break of 10 or 15 years, the bond dies," he said. FINANCIAL TRAP Few embody the frustrations of reconstruction more than brother and sister Alfredo and Elisabetta Perilli. They lost many relatives and their respective homes in the centre of Amatrice. Alfredo still has to pay the mortgage on his old house, trapping him financially. "The building no longer exists, but the bank wants its money every month," he said. The Perillis also lost their family-run restaurant and hotel, with the land it once occupied now serving as a temporary access route for the reconstruction of a hospital. Building work was scheduled to finish in 2022. Until they get their site back, they cannot submit reconstruction plans for approval. "If they go on much longer I won't have the strength to start rebuilding," said Elisabetta. Such delays have left Cortellesi wondering whether some of the choices made after the earthquake were the right ones, including the core decision to recreate much of the town on its original site and largely in its former image. "What we will have is a facsimile," he said, acknowledging that much of the medieval masonry had gone. "Personally, I would have redesigned the town in a modern way. Once everything had been wiped away, I think something new could have been created, but it is too late to turn back."

item.title: Treasury's upsized buybacks may complicate Fed's monetary policy work
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh has promised that the U.S. central bank will deliver price stability, but Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's decision on Wednesday to double buybacks of longer-dated U.S. debt may complicate any effort to do so.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby, Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh has promised that the U.S. central bank will deliver price stability, but Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's decision on Wednesday to double buybacks of longer-dated U.S. debt may complicate any effort to do so. On Wednesday, the Treasury Department announced that it was [USN:FWN44G0QP TEXT:"doubling"] the size of its effort to buy back Treasury securities with maturities between 10 and 30 years, to $4 billion per operation. The government announced this as long-dated Treasury borrowing costs have been moving up sharply, negatively impacting credit affordability in the global economy generally. The Treasury announcement helped bring yields, which move inversely to prices, [USN:L8N44G129 TEXT:"down"] in trading that followed the announcement. Its action has generated questions as to whether the Fed or the Treasury is now the bigger influence on general credit conditions. "Given Warsh’s desire to say less and [Treasury Secretary Scott] Bessent’s actions today, the center of gravity could be moving from the Fed to the Treasury. We’ll have to see if this continues because it would be a big change for traders," said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation. Since the global financial crisis two decades ago the central bank has used asset buying to calm markets and to lower long-term borrowing costs. The rise in Treasury bond yields has been jarring to market observers and has raised questions as to whether the situation is extreme enough for the Fed to get involved, even as there are lots of questions about the longer-term potency of the new Treasury buyback schedule. Warsh has long expressed skepticism over using central bank asset buying as a policy tool, and has made as a cornerstone goal getting what is now a $6.8 trillion balance sheet lower. But he has also signaled a willingness to work with the Treasury and coordinate where possible, which might make the Fed leader more open to link up with the Treasury despite his broader disdain for large Fed holdings. How Warsh could act is further complicated by his near blanket refusal to explain what he thinks lies ahead for monetary policy and his unwillingness to provide much guidance on how he looks at data to reach policy decisions. HIGH BAR Thus far, market participants don’t see a case for Fed involvement. “The bar for the Fed to step in with market-stabilizing purchases is very high at the moment and we would need to see signs of liquidity deteriorating enormously and signs of market dysfunction, which we're simply not seeing,” said Gennadiy Goldberg, Head of U.S. Rates Strategy at TD Securities. Most importantly, the market is functioning in a way that the Fed can still manage its interest rate target range, which meeting minutes from the late July Federal Open Market Committee, released Wednesday, affirmed is the central bank’s main tool to achieve its job and inflation mandates. “I don’t see any impact on the Fed's ability to control short-term interest rates,” said Michael Feroli, chief U.S. economist at J.P. Morgan. The range of debt targeted by the Treasury increased buyback operation is very influential to real world borrowing costs for things like mortgages and corporate borrowing. Borrowing costs for the long bond hit nearly a two-decade high amid concerns about inflation, government borrowing appetites, and as the Treasury faces competition from the offerings from companies furiously building out infrastructure for artificial intelligence. Presumably Fed asset buying could lower those yields or cap their rise, and it would have more firepower to devote to the matter than the Treasury. But as it would be akin to an easing of monetary policy and that would be hard to square against the Fed’s ongoing efforts to lower inflation that still stands well above the 2% target. Daleep Singh, chief global economist at PGIM, who also served at the New York Fed and Treasury Department, said what the Treasury has done ultimately doesn't change the story driving yields up and while its action is shining a spotlight on a real issue it is doing so "without a credible strategy to solve" the issue. SHRINKAGE The size of Fed holdings matters to Warsh because he believes the Fed owns too many bonds and that those holdings distort financial market pricing. He wants the Fed to own fewer bonds but has said that will take time to achieve that given the complexity of the issue. At the June FOMC meeting he announced a series of task forces weighing Fed issues and one of them was devoted to tackling Fed balance sheet issues. There is broad speculation the Fed may be able to get its holdings smaller by changes in banking rules that would permit banks to hold less emergency liquidity, though some fear that could increase financial stability risks and force the Fed to intervene more often in times of stress.

item.title: HKEX diversification drive has a focus problem
item.description: The $67 bln bourse's record earnings relied on equities surging past 50% of revenue. It seems counter to CEO Bonnie Chan's goal to be a big player in bonds, currencies, commodities and indices. Picking just one or two, perhaps with some M&A help, could speed up the process.
item.dc:creator: Hudson Lockett
item.content:encoded: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (0388.HK) suffers from both a lack and excess of ambition. CEO Bonnie Chan acknowledges the $67 billion bourse’s over-reliance on its equities business and wants to create what she calls a multi-asset ecosystem. But those plans lack focus. A more concrete growth roadmap would buoy lacklustre shares. Chan, who was this week reappointed for a second three-year term starting in March, has hit some of her other marks. She has diligently ensured the exchange capitalised on a rebound in trading and equity fundraising in Hong Kong, helping boost first-half net income in 2026 by a fifth to a record HK$10.6 billion ($1.4 billion). And on Wednesday she stressed that the exchange needs to diversify beyond its stock market. Yet cash equities’ share of revenue has risen from 40% to 53% under her watch. Meanwhile, HKEX's own stock trades at 27 times forward earnings, well below an historical average of 32 times. Analysts at Citi argue the stock should already be close to that higher multiple based on their forecast that average daily trading turnover could pip market expectations by up to 11% over the coming years. That shares are up less than 2% so far this year suggests investors are wary of another trading slump and doubt diversification will pay off - probably due to a lack of detail on building bond, fixed income, currency, commodities and index businesses. Those plans face obstacles beyond her control. Anything related to the yuan requires Beijing’s approval to meaningfully scale up. Running a post-trade custody business could be lucrative, but HKEX only owns 20% of CMU OmniClear , the markets infrastructure firm central to the endeavour. And an initiative to build an index business from scratch looks quixotic given the dominance of benchmark provider Hang Seng Indexes. Chan would be better off narrowing her sights to a couple of options at most — preferably ones where HKEX can exert total control — and then executing at speed. M&A would be quickest, if done properly. The company has $2.7 billion of cash it can tap and, with only a sliver of debt, plenty of room to borrow. Buying Hang Seng Indexes from HSBC-owned (HSBA.L) , (0005.HK) Hang Seng Bank is one obvious starting option. This would give the exchange a market-leading position, allowing it to focus next on whichever other business line looks most promising. As long as the price were right, it would be simple, clean and bring HKEX in line with its benchmark-owning global peers. What’s not to like? Follow Hudson Lockett on Bluesky and X . Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing on August 19 posted record net income for the first half of the year of HK$10.6 billion, up 24% from the same period last year. Overall revenue increased 19% to HK$16.7 billion, while core business revenue rose by the same extent to HK$15.5 billion on the back of an 18% rise in average daily turnover and a surge in equity fundraising activity. item.title: China boosts imports of Russian crude, stymieing India's refiners
item.description: One of the balancing acts that has prevented crude oil prices from spiking higher during the Iran war has been India buying record volumes of Russian crude.
item.dc:creator: Clyde Russell
item.content:encoded: One of the balancing acts that has prevented crude oil prices from spiking higher during the Iran war has been India buying record volumes of Russian crude. But it's getting more challenging for the world's third-biggest crude importer as top-ranked China resumes buying more from Russia amid the ongoing supply disruptions sparked by the conflict. China's imports of seaborne Russian crude in August are estimated at 1.25 million barrels per day (bpd) by commodity analysts Kpler, down slightly from 1.423 million bpd in July. However, July and August were the two strongest months for China's seaborne imports from Russia since April and show that China's refiners are seeking more Russian cargoes to replace barrels from the Middle East. China has been the biggest buyer of Russian and Iranian crude in recent years as it was prepared to ignore U.S. and Western sanctions against the two producers. But the Middle East conflict and the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports have resulted in sharply lower Chinese imports of Iranian crude, with Kpler estimating August arrivals at around 340,000 bpd. This is roughly in line with July's 329,000 bpd and June's 361,000 bpd, but the past three months are about a third of the 1.14 million bpd of Iranian oil that China imported in March. That March crude would have left Iran before the U.S. and Israel launched their aerial attacks on February 28, with the strikes prompting Tehran to effectively close the Strait of Hormuz to vessels through missile and drone strikes. Nearly 20% of the world's crude oil and refined products moved through the narrow waterway before the conflict began, and while volumes have recovered in recent weeks they are still well below pre-war levels. China usually sources the bulk of its Russian seaborne oil from the country's eastern ports, which supply the ESPO grade, rather than Russia's ports in Europe, which largely ship Urals crude. China also imports just under 1 million bpd of Russian crude via pipelines. For example, in July 90% of China's imports of seaborne Russian crude were sourced from Asian ports, while in June it was 78%. However, for August Kpler data shows that the share of crude from Russia's European ports is rising to 31%. That matters for India, which generally receives the bulk of its Russian crude from European ports. INDIA GETS LESS RUSSIAN OIL India's total imports of Russian crude are estimated at 1.87 million bpd in August, down from 2.79 million bpd in July and 2.73 million bpd in June. July and June were the two strongest months on record for India's imports from Russia, exceeding the 1.21 million bpd average for the three months leading up to the start of the Iran war. In July, India's imports from Russia's European ports were 93.4% of its total and were 2.59 million bpd. For August, the percentage has gone up to 97.4% as China takes more of Russia's Asian crude. But more importantly for India's refiners, the volume of imports from Russia's European ports is estimated at 1.82 million bpd in August, down almost 30% or about 770,000 bpd. This is showing up in India's total crude imports, which are estimated by Kpler at 4.17 million bpd for August, the lowest since the Iran conflict started and down from 5.06 million in July. It's likely that India's August imports will be revised higher as more cargoes are assessed before the end of the month, but even so it's still clear that India is struggling to find enough crude to replace Russian barrels that are now heading to China. This could have a potential flow-on effect for Asia's already tight markets for refined products given India is a major exporter of diesel and gasoline. India's August exports of light and middle distillates are estimated at 1.29 million bpd, the same as for July and the two strongest months since September last year. However, any shortage of crude for India's refiners will only show up from September onwards, and if this does result in lower fuel exports, it will exacerbate the mounting supply crisis in Asia.
